title: A good address. But at what price?
videoTitle: ASKING SEAN #239 | "LOCATION LOCATION LOCATION" STILL VALID?
excerpt: A conversation about Bangsar South puts the purchase price back into the property equation.
takeaways: The discussion includes a young investor and Bangsar South.
Sean stresses entry price alongside location.
Cash flow and appreciation are different objectives.

sections.heading: The address is only part of the question
paragraphs: Sean's episode notes describe a 26-year-old viewer with a high-income career and an existing portfolio who is considering real estate. Bangsar South features prominently in the conversation.

sections.heading: The price changes the proposition
paragraphs: Sean challenges the idea that location alone settles an investment decision. His stated position is that an appropriately priced property in an ordinary location can be preferable to an overpriced property in a desirable one. This is his framework, rather than a valuation of any current listing.

sections.heading: Two different kinds of return
paragraphs: The notes also distinguish capital appreciation from cash flow. Sean presents the balance between them as a matter of the investor's priorities, even though having both would be attractive.

closing: Use the episode to frame questions about a purchase, then assess those questions using current, property-specific evidence.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's published episode notes. Full captions were unavailable; no returns, valuation figures or detailed case-study numbers have been inferred.
